MM5P-N03.free_elimination: 0.6 m of ribbon costs less than one full meter ($7.25), so total < 7.25 + 2(1.70) = 10.65; D is exactly that cap and is struck.
MM5P-N03.error_directions: 7.85: arithmetic slip (e.g. 4.45 + 3.40), above, not predictable. 8.05: slip in 7.25 x 0.6 (4.65 + 3.40), above, not predictable. 10.65: ignores the 0.6 and uses $7.25 for the ribbon, above; stem lets a student see this as the full-meter cap.
MM5P-N03.interior_parity: 7.85 and 8.05: same form (two-decimal dollar amounts); key is not interior.
MM5P-N03.grade_note: Grade 5 decimal multiplication (hundredths x tenths) plus a whole-number multiple and a sum; a standard two-step grade-5 item, typical rather than hard.
MM5P-N03.note: 7.25 x 0.6 = 4.35; 2 x 1.70 = 3.40; total 7.75. Key is the smallest option but distractor errors are not predictably above.
MM5P-N03.key_note: 0.6 x 7.25 = 4.35, plus 3.40 = 7.75; matches my stage-1 answer.
MM5P-N03.path_note: B: 4.20 + 0.25 + 3.40 = 7.85 checks. C: 4.35 + 3.70 = 8.05 checks (adding 2 instead of multiplying by 2 is a less common slip but real). D: 7.25 + 3.40 = 10.65 checks. My stage-1 guesses for B and C differed from the stated paths, but the values agree.
MM5P-N03.grade_note_final: A standard grade-5 decimal two-step; I would label it mid, not high. Fix the tier rather than drop.

MM5P-N10.error_directions: 238: subtracts 5 x 10 = 50 (misreads 2^2 as 10 or doubles wrongly) from 288, below, not predictable. 188: subtracts 100 (5^2 x 4 or 5 x 20), below, not predictable. 128: takes 2^7 alone / drops the 9 and the deletion, below, not predictable.
MM5P-N10.interior_parity: 188 and 238: same form (three-digit whole numbers ending in 8); key is not interior.
MM5P-N10.arith_tell: 268 alone has option + 20 a multiple of 9 (stem: 9 x 2^k minus 5 x 2^2 = 20)
MM5P-N10.grade_note: 8.EE.1 product of powers with a negative exponent, then simple arithmetic; easy grade-8 exponent item.
MM5P-N10.note: 2^7 x 2^-2 = 2^5 = 32; 9 x 32 = 288; 5 x 4 = 20; 288 - 20 = 268. Key is the largest option; all distractors below, but the stem does not tell a student errors go low (natural errors like 2^9 or forgetting to subtract go high and are absent). Divisibility tell (option+20 divisible by 9) exists but costs about as much as the work.
MM5P-N10.path_note: A: (5x2)^2 = 100 gives 188. C: 5^2 x 2 = 50 gives 238. D: (9-5) x 2^5 = 128. All check, and all are real exponent errors. Stage-1 guesses for A and D differed from the stated paths; the values agree.
MM5P-N10.grade_note_final: Easy 8.EE.1 item; low tier is right. The divisibility tell (option + 20 a multiple of 9) costs as much as solving.

MM5P-N11.error_directions: 1000: adds the densities 700 + 300 instead of subtracting, above, predictable only after the work. 420: subtracts populations first, (8.4 - 4.2) x 10^6 / 10^4, above, not predictable. 520: unclear slip (e.g. wrong density for B), above, not predictable.
MM5P-N11.interior_parity: 420 and 520: same form (whole numbers); key is not interior.
MM5P-N11.grade_note: 8.EE.4 division in scientific notation in a rate context, two quotients and a difference; typical grade 8.
MM5P-N11.note: A: 8.4/1.2 = 7, 10^2 -> 700. B: 4.2/1.4 = 3 -> 300. Difference 400. Key smallest; errors not predictably above.
MM5P-N11.path_note: A: 700 + 300 = 1000 checks. B: '8/1 = 8, 0.4/0.2 = 2, so 8.2' gives 820 - 300 = 520; it checks arithmetically, but this piecewise decimal division is a contrived error. D: dividing correctly for A and subtracting for B is an inconsistent error (280, so 420); it checks but is unlikely.
MM5P-N11.grade_note_final: Typical 8.EE.4 rate item. B and D are on the contrived side, but 1000 is a real error and none of the options leaks the key.

MM5P-N02.error_directions: 3 5/12: regrouping slip in 5 3/12 - 1 8/12, below, not predictable. 3 1/12: multiplication slip in 9/4 x 7/3 (e.g. 4 3/4 area), below, not predictable. 2 11/12: subtracts an extra 2/3 or uses a smaller area, below, not predictable.
MM5P-N02.interior_parity: 3 1/12 and 3 5/12: same form (mixed numbers in twelfths); key is not interior.
MM5P-N02.grade_note: 5.NF.4/5.NF.6 area with mixed-number factors, then subtraction of unlike-denominator mixed numbers with regrouping; grade-5 content at typical difficulty.
MM5P-N02.note: 9/4 x 7/3 = 63/12 = 5 1/4; 5 3/12 - 1 8/12 = 3 7/12. Key largest; distractors all below but the stem gives no direction. Borderline pair: 3 7/12 and 2 11/12 differ by 2/3, the fractional part of printed 1 2/3 (not a printed number itself, so null).
MM5P-N02.path_note: A: partial products missing 1/4 x 2 give 4 3/4, so 3 1/12; checks. B: base-ten borrow 4 13/12 - 1 8/12 = 3 5/12; checks. C: perimeter-style sum 4 7/12 - 1 8/12 = 2 11/12; checks. All are classic grade-5 errors. Stage 1 noted that 3 7/12 and 2 11/12 differ by 2/3; the stated path for C is the sum, not an extra 2/3, so it is a coincidence.
MM5P-N02.grade_note_final: Grade-5 mixed-number multiplication with subtraction and regrouping; mid tier, with good distractors.

MM5P-N06.free_elimination: A lap is less than 1 mile, so laps > track miles (about 10); 4 7/12 is struck by that bound. Laps of 3/5 mile mean about 5/3 laps per mile, so roughly 17 laps; 10 5/12 (barely more than the miles) is struck by magnitude. 16 11/12 vs 17 1/12 needs the work.
MM5P-N06.error_directions: 16 11/12: divides only the whole part, 10 x 5/3 + 1/4 = 16 2/3 + 1/4, below. 10 5/12: scales only the fraction, 10 + 1/4 x 5/3, below. 4 7/12: muddled operation (e.g. multiplies by 3/5 and slips), below. The stem (dividing by a fraction less than 1 enlarges) lets a student predict partial-scaling errors fall low.
MM5P-N06.extreme_single_bound: laps > 10 1/4 because a lap is shorter than a mile
MM5P-N06.interior_parity: 10 5/12 and 16 11/12: same form (mixed numbers in twelfths); key is not interior.
MM5P-N06.grade_note: 6.NS.1 division of a mixed number by a fraction after a subtraction step, answer a mixed number; harder-than-typical grade 6.
MM5P-N06.note: 10 1/2 - 1/4 = 41/4; 41/4 / 3/5 = 205/12 = 17 1/12. Key largest; all distractors below via under-scaling errors. Plug-back possible (option x 3/5 + 1/4 = 10 1/2) but four fraction multiplications ascending, not routine.
MM5P-N06.path_note: B: 10 + (1/4)/(3/5) = 10 5/12 checks. C: 16 2/3 + 1/4 = 16 11/12 checks. D: 11/4 x 5/3 = 55/12 = 4 7/12 checks. Stage-1 guess for D differed from the stated path; the value agrees.
MM5P-N06.drop_reason: One-sided. All three distractors are under-scaling errors, so they all fall below the key, and the key is the largest option. A student who knows that dividing by 3/5 makes the number bigger can 'pick the largest' and win. Also, 4 7/12 is struck by the bound 'a lap is shorter than a mile' and 10 5/12 by magnitude, so only 16 11/12 vs 17 1/12 needs any work. Repair: add a distractor above the key (e.g. not subtracting the 1/4, giving 17 1/2) in place of 4 7/12.
MM5P-N06.grade_note_final: 6.NS.1 fraction division after a subtraction; high tier is right. The drop is for the option set, not the grade.

MM5P-N05.error_directions: 5 3/8: regrouping error in 7 4/8 - 2 7/8 (subtracts 4/8 from 7/8, 7 - 2), above, not predictable. 4 7/8: fraction slip in the same subtraction, above, not predictable. 6 3/8: places P or combines distances wrongly, above, not predictable.
MM5P-N05.interior_parity: 4 7/8 and 5 3/8: same form (mixed numbers in eighths); key is not interior.
MM5P-N05.grade_note: Negative mixed-number positions, moving left, then distance with regrouping across unlike denominators; rational-number subtraction/distance is 7.NS.1, so for grade 6 this is a high item, not mid.
MM5P-N05.note: P = -6 1/4 - 1 1/4 = -7 1/2; distance to -2 7/8 = 7 4/8 - 2 7/8 = 4 5/8. Key smallest; errors not predictably above. 4 5/8 and 4 7/8 differ by 1/4 (fractional part of printed numbers, not a printed number itself, so null).
MM5P-N05.path_note: A: base-ten borrow 6 14/8 - 2 7/8 = 4 7/8 checks. C: smaller-from-larger 5 3/8 checks. D: Q misread as -1 1/8, so 7 1/2 - 1 1/8 = 6 3/8 checks. All are real errors. Stage-1 guess for D differed from the stated path; the value agrees.
MM5P-N05.grade_note_final: Distance between two same-sign points is grade-6 content (6.NS.8, via absolute values), so stage 1 was too strong in calling it grade-7 (7.NS.1) material. But placing a negative mixed number, then subtracting with regrouping in eighths, makes it a high item, not mid. Retier rather than drop.
